findings.issue_text: [BUG] The light-theme branch was changed from scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) to scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), inverting the light theme's username emphasis instead of only adding a dark branch. Light-theme users get pale, low-contrast usernames in the small-action row (used for like/flag counts and usernames) — the 70% lightened color sits barely above the background — while the dark branch (30%) is unchanged relative to intent; every other hunk in this diff preserves the light-side value, so this is a copy-paste of the wrong argument.

[BUG] The light branch of .staff .name/.name color was changed from scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) to 50%, altering light-theme rendering rather than only adding a dark-theme alternative. Light-theme user cards show names at 50% lightness instead of the previous 30%, reducing the visual weight of usernames on user pages; every other hunk in this PR keeps the light-side value identical, so this breaks the stated purpose of the change (only dark themes should look different).

[BUG] Same light-branch mutation as desktop: .name color changes from scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) to 50% in the light branch, changing light-theme appearance. Mobile light-theme user pages render names at the wrong lightness (50% vs previous 30%), an unintended regression of the light theme identical to the desktop/user.scss slip.

[BUG] The light branch of .custom-message-length was inverted from scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%) to 30%, unlike the desktop/modal.scss counterpart which correctly preserves 70% in the light branch. Mobile light-theme modals render the custom-message-length hint at 30% lightness (near-solid, visually heavier than body text) instead of the previous subtle 70%, and mobile/desktop now disagree; the asymmetry with desktop/modal.scss line 94 confirms the arguments were swapped.

[BUG] The light branch of the h3 color inside a.star was changed from scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%) to 50%, changing light-theme rendering. Mobile light-theme link-preview titles drop from strong 20% lightness to a washed-out 50%, unlike desktop/topic-post.scss line 321 which correctly preserves 20% — a copy-paste error in the light argument.

[BUG] The light-theme branch value was silently changed from 30% to 70%: `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%);` became `color: dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%));`. On light themes, the usernames/links in this block (the gap between post numbers / arrow section) render at 70% lightness instead of the previous 30%, a visually obvious unintended regression on the untouched (light) side of the conversion; only the dark branch was supposed to change.

[BUG] The light-theme branch value was changed from 30% to 50%: `.name { color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%);` became `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), ...)`. User-card names on light themes render noticeably lighter than before, an unintended light-theme regression; common/base/user.scss (line ~126) keeps the same selector at 30%, so the two files now disagree on the same element's light-theme color.

[BUG] The light-theme branch value was changed from 30% to 50% for `.name`: `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%);` became `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), ...)`. Mobile user-card names on light themes render lighter than before, diverging from the equivalent unchanged 30% rule in common/base/user.scss — an unintended light-theme regression parallel to the desktop one.

[BUG] The light-theme branch value was changed from 20% to 50% for the h3 in the mobile link-summary/small-action block: `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%);` became `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), ...)`. Mobile link-summary headings on light themes render at half the previous contrast; desktop/topic-post.scss (line ~318) keeps the identical selector at 20%, so mobile and desktop now disagree — the light branch was supposed to be a pure wrap.

[BUG] The light-theme branch value was inverted from 70% to 30%: `.custom-message-length` color `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)` became `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`. Mobile custom-message-length hints on light themes render far darker than before (30% vs 70%), while desktop/modal.scss (line ~50) keeps the same rule at 70%/30% dark — the mobile light branch is flipped, an unintended light-theme regression.

[ADVISORY] Sibling declarations on the same touched composer path were left as raw scale-color($primary, ...) with no dark-light-choose wrapper: line 33's context `color: scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%);` and the `.wmd-input { color: darken($primary, 40%); }` rule below. Dark-theme users get unconverted (and for darken($primary, 40%), actively worse) colors in the mobile composer while surrounding rules were fixed, leaving a visibly inconsistent patchwork in the very screen this diff touches.

[ADVISORY] This is a mechanical 60+-site string replacement with no tests, no visual regression verification, and at least five light-branch value changes (see the bug findings), indicating the sweep was not verified per-site. Reviewers and users on default light themes absorb the five unintended color changes above because nothing in the diff distinguishes an intentional light-theme change from a find/replace typo; the missing acceptance criterion is that every light branch value must be byte-identical to the pre-diff value.

[BUG] This hunk silently changes the light-theme value, not just the dark-theme fallback: `.small-action .list-mod ... a` previously used scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) and now uses scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%). Light-scheme sites get a much lighter link color for the small-action moderator links than before this PR — an unrelated visual regression that is invisible unless someone diffs light theme before/after; the stated intent was to only add the dark-theme $secondary branch.

[BUG] The .name rule's light-theme branch was changed from scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) to scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), altering light-theme output outside the stated intent. User profile display names render 20 lightness-points lighter on light themes after this PR, degrading contrast for a text element the requirement never asked to change; this is implementation work not traceable to the stated intent.

[BUG] The mobile .name rule's light branch was changed from 30% to 50% lightness, mirroring an apparent copy-paste of the adjacent .title rule rather than the mechanical $primary/$secondary conversion. Mobile user display names on light themes lose contrast after this change; any reviewer approving 'only dark-theme fallback additions' ships an unrequested light-theme restyle to production.

[BUG] The h3 inside the topic-list onebox changed its light-theme value from scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%) to 50%, while the parallel desktop rule (desktop/topic-post.scss ~line 320) correctly keeps 20%. Mobile onebox titles render at 50% lightness while desktop renders the same element at 20%, creating a mobile/desktop visual divergence introduced by this diff, and again an unrequested light-theme change; desktop parity shows this is a transcription error, not intent.

[BUG] .custom-message-length changed its light-theme branch from 70% to 30% lightness, inverting the value, while the identical desktop rule (desktop/modal.scss ~line 94) keeps 70% for the light branch. Mobile custom-message-length hint text becomes near-black on light themes while desktop keeps the intended 70% gray, a mobile-only light-theme regression introduced alongside a change that claims to only add dark-theme fallbacks.

[ADVISORY] The coldmap-* dark-theme values use scale-color($secondary, ...) with reversed lightness (70%/60%/50% → 30%/40%/50%), which is correct inversion, but the hunk leaves the adjacent comment "// is scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%)" describing the old formula while the code no longer matches it. The next theming contributor reading this comment will reproduce the pre-PR single-color formula and silently undo the dark-theme fix; this is stale-comment drift created by this diff's own edit.

[BUG] The `.name` rule's light-theme branch was silently changed from 30% lightness to 50% lightness, breaking the established inversion pattern used everywhere else in this diff. On light themes the user profile name renders noticeably lighter than before the PR (and lighter than the `.username a` rule directly above, which correctly uses 30%), and the dark branch 50% does not invert to the 70% every other 30% rule in this diff uses; light-theme users see an unintended visual regression in the user card/profile.

[BUG] Mobile `.name` was converted as dark-light-choose(50%, 50%) from scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), changing the light-theme value from 30% to 50% and the dark value from the pattern-consistent 70% to 50%. Mobile light-theme users see the profile name lighter than the paired `.username a` (unchanged context) and than desktop; the mobile and desktop renderings of the same component drift because desktop got 50%/50% here too but the original design intent (30% lightness, per the common/base/user.scss counterpart) is lost.

[BUG] The nav.post-controls ... `a` rule was changed from scale-color($primary, 30%) to dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, 70%), scale-color($secondary, 30%)) — the light-theme branch jumped from 30% to 70% instead of staying 30%. On light themes these post-control links (e.g. the small 'x replies' links) become washed out and low-contrast against the light background; the correct conversion per this PR's own pattern is (30%, 70%).

[BUG] The mobile `a.star h3` rule was converted from scale-color($primary, 20%) to dark-light-choose(50%, 50%), changing the light-theme branch from 20% to 50% instead of the pattern-consistent (20%, 80%). Light-theme mobile users get a much lighter, lower-contrast external-link title than before the PR and than the desktop counterpart (desktop a.star h3 keeps 20%/80%); the element that was designed as high-emphasis text loses that emphasis.

[BUG] Mobile `.custom-message-length` was converted to dark-light-choose(30%, 70%) while the desktop/modal.scss conversion of the identical rule uses dark-light-choose(70%, 30%), inverting the light/dark branches on mobile. On light-theme mobile the custom-message-length hint renders dark (30%) instead of the intended light 70% hint gray, and on dark themes it renders bright instead of dim — mobile and desktop now disagree on the same component, so one of the two is wrong on both schemes.

[ADVISORY] The coldmap classes now hardcode dark-light-choose with per-level hand-tuned lightness pairs (70/30, 60/40, 50/50) duplicating a scheme that must stay ordered, while the comment above ('numbers get dimmer as they get colder') describes only the light-theme direction. The next theme-variable change (e.g. a color-scheme overhaul adding a third scheme or renaming $secondary) requires touching dozens of scattered dark-light-choose pairs across ~25 files with no single source; a missed one produces an invisible dark-theme regression exactly like the ones above, and the diff itself already contains five transcription errors, which is the demonstrated failure mode of this hand-copy approach.

[BUG] The light-theme branch was inverted: .custom-message-length changes from scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%) to scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), which is not the mechanical dark-light-choose wrapping the PR title describes. On light themes the custom message length hint renders at 30% lightness (much darker, near-black) instead of the previous 70% muted gray, silently changing light-theme appearance while mobile and desktop equivalents diverge (desktop/modal.scss keeps 70% for the same selector).

[BUG] The h3 inside a.small-action changes its light-theme value from scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%) to scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%) instead of preserving 20% as the first argument. Light-theme users see the small-action heading at 50% lightness instead of the intended near-full-contrast 20%, a visual regression beyond the stated dark-theme-only change; it also diverges from desktop/topic-post.scss h3 which keeps 20%.

[BUG] The nested a in small-action changes its light-theme color from scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) to scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), flipping the intended emphasis. On light themes this bold link becomes 70% lightness (very washed out) instead of 30%, reducing contrast and breaking the visual hierarchy for that element; likely the two dark-light-choose arguments were swapped.

[BUG] The .name element's light-theme color changes from scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) to scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%) instead of preserving the original value. Light-theme user names in the profile header lose the stronger 30% emphasis and render at the same muted 50% as .title, flattening the intended hierarchy; also diverges from common/base/user.scss which correctly preserves 30% for the same element.

[BUG] The .name element's light-theme color changes from scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) to scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), altering light-theme behavior beyond adding a dark variant. Mobile light-theme user names render at 50% lightness instead of 30%, losing the intended stronger emphasis relative to .title and creating desktop/mobile inconsistency with common/base/user.scss.

[BUG] The light-theme argument was changed from 30% to 70% in .who-liked a, inverting the intended emphasis: every other block in this diff preserves the original $primary lightness and only adds the $secondary fallback. On light themes, the names of users who liked a post render at 70% lightness instead of 30%, making them near-invisible faint gray text; the PR that promised only dark-theme fixes silently regressed light-theme readability.

[BUG] The light-theme argument was changed from 70% to 30% in .custom-message-length, the inverse of the matching desktop/modal.scss rule (which keeps 70%), producing an unintended light-theme change. Mobile users on light themes see the custom-message character counter at 30% lightness — dark, heavy text instead of the subtle 70% hint — while desktop keeps the correct styling, creating a visible mobile/desktop divergence the PR never intended to introduce.

[BUG] The light-theme argument for .name was changed from 30% to 50% while the .title sibling below it kept 50%, indicating a copy-paste slip rather than an intentional re-tuning of light-theme values. User profile full names on light themes lose their previous 30% contrast level against the 50% title, flattening the intended visual hierarchy; the identical slip recurs at mobile/user.scss:494-499.

[BUG] The light-theme argument for the a.star h3 selector was changed from 20% to 50% while the parallel desktop/topic-post.scss h3 rule (line 318-321) kept its original 20%, so this is an unintended edit to the light-theme value, not the dark-theme fallback. Mobile light-theme users see the small-action heading (e.g. likes/bookmarks headings) at 50% lightness instead of the intended 20% bold-contrast value, while desktop retains the stronger color — a mobile-only visual regression unrelated to the PR's stated dark-theme purpose.
